findings.title: Rejecting an existing run root can overwrite its prior failure evidence
findings.body: source_probe.run rejects an existing output_root before creating any new artifacts (source_probe.py:40), but runner.main catches that FileExistsError and writes output_root/failure.json whenever summary.json is absent. Reinvoking the normal fixed command on a partial or failed immutable run therefore replaces its original failure.json with the output-collision error, despite the preservation refusal.
findings.required_fix: Write failure.json only for an output root newly created and owned by this invocation; leave a pre-existing root and all its artifacts unchanged when rejecting it.

targeted_fix_review.scope: Only the previously reported output-ownership P1; no full re-review
targeted_fix_review.resolved_finding: Pre-existing output roots are rejected without writing or replacing their failure artifacts.

code_evidence.observation: Calls run(request) directly; no exception handler writes into a rejected existing root.
mkdir(exist_ok=False) executes before the owned-run try/except. An existing root exits before the failure writer.
Only the successfully created output root reaches the failure writer, which uses exclusive mode x.

focused_regression.evidence_source: Root-reported three passing output_checks; test source inspected in this targeted review, not rerun
cases: new owned failure and partial artifacts retained
